verdict.stance: Constructive / Deleveraging South African Energy & Chemicals Producer (BB+ Neg / Ba1 Neg)
verdict.summary: Sasol's FY26 (Jun-26) audited results showed strong deleveraging: revenue rose 9% to R272.1bn, Adj EBITDA jumped 17% to R60.7bn, capex fell 18% to R20.9bn, FCF reached R11.9bn, and net debt ex-leases declined 11% YoY to $3.3bn (~0.96x Adj EBITDA) backed by R43.3bn cash.

positives: FY26 deleveraging beat: Net debt ex-leases fell 11% YoY to $3,259M (well inside <$3.7bn threshold); Adj EBITDA +17% to R60.7bn.
Creditor-friendly capital allocation: No final dividend paid while net debt remains above the $3.0bn policy trigger.
Strong liquidity buffer (~$5bn) and operating cash flow up 22% YoY to R56.7bn in FY26.
negatives: Thin FCF generation: FY26 FCF was R11.9bn (-5% YoY) due to working capital build; hitting <$3.0bn net debt depends on Brent and WC reversal.
Negative rating outlooks: Moody's Ba1 Neg and S&P BB+ Neg reflect oil/chemical cyclicality and carbon transition capex.
Operational risks: Natref outage/Prax uncertainty, weak gas EBIT (-60%), Secunda impairment, and disclosed internal control weaknesses.
